The one-line fix for alg:none: pass `algorithms=["HS256"]` explicitly to `jwt.decode()`. PyJWT then rejects any token whose header declares a different algorithm — `none`, `NONE`, or `None` — before it even looks at the signature.

For `issue_jwt`, build a payload dict with `sub`, `iss`, `aud`, `iat=int(time.time())`, and `exp=iat+900`. Then call `jwt.encode(payload, SECRET_KEY, algorithm="HS256")`. For `verify_jwt`, pass `audience=AUDIENCE` and `issuer=ISSUER` to `jwt.decode()` — the library validates both claims for you.

Force all required claims to exist: `options={"require": ["exp", "iat", "iss", "aud", "sub"]}` in `jwt.decode()`. Without this, a token with no `exp` (infinite lifetime) passes the expiry check because there's nothing to check.
